announced on Friday that it signed a non-binding LOI to acquire its first U.S. data center.
The acquisition is targeted to be completed by the end of November 2026.
The existing facility has 6 MW of current power capacity, with a potential expansion to 36 MW.
Moreover, the local utility supports an additional 30 MW of power, expected to be delivered in about 18 months, subject to infrastructure work.
The operational facility generates colocation revenue, which the company expects to continue after the acquisition, subject to final lease and transfer arrangements.
The company targets a U.S. data center portfolio exceeding 100 MW within 12–18 months through acquisitions, expansion, and AI computing deployments.
The deal remains subject to due diligence and definitive agreements.

title: Gorilla eyes 100 MW portfolio after first U.S. data center LOI
